summary: Shiro Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Waseda, Komazawa, and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served on the faculty at Komazawa University from 1982, becoming professor in 1995 until 2020.

Shiv Nath Sharma worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947) and as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, later serving as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University and department head at Deccan College.

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University under Jikido Takasaki, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University. In 1990 he joined Hanazono University, becoming Professor of Indian Buddhism in 2002.

Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin, taught at the University of Paris and the Institut d'Histoire des Sciences et des Techniques, and was a philosophy professor at Hebrew University.

Shmuel Sambursky was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Berlin and the University of Königsberg before holding an academic post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1928 to 1970.

Shobha Rani Dash is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010, a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied at Shofuku-ji under Mumon Yamada from 1962 to 1982, became abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982, and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamagami is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto Sangyo University as an associate professor (circa 1978–1988) and as a professor (circa 1988–2010).

Shogo Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University, where he taught from circa 1989 and served as professor from circa 2002 to 2024, later affiliating with Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Taisho University.

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He founded the Sanshin Zen Community and Pioneer Valley Zendo, and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa was a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1949 to 1952 and held a post at The Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, worked at the Okurayama Institute, and served as associate professor (circa 1978–1988) and professor (circa 1988–2009) at Toyo University.
Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1958 to 1981 and also worked as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1952 to 1957. He held academic posts at Ueno Gakuen University (circa 1963–1979) and Otani University (circa 1979–1998).

Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo University and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido University and Nihon University, and became director of Matsugaoka Bunko in 1966.
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Toyo University (attested in 1987 and 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed his undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University. He joined Taisho University as a lecturer in 1960 and served as Dean of Buddhist Studies from 1978 to 2002.

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata holds lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
